text:
maya: quick async standup — kernel + batching + KV warmup status. TL;DR: perf improving overall but seeing p99 tail on seq>1024 when cache miss rate creeps above ~15%. details below.

ken: saw the same on staging earlier. traced a hot path to a tokenizer lock in the kernel. adding a few more debug logs now. can you paste the bench command you used?

maya: bench cmd: `./bench --model galactica --seq 4096 --concurrency 8 --microbatch 2` ; results this morning: mean ~42ms/token, p95 ~120ms, p99 ~230–300ms. when KV hit rate >85% p99 drops to ~60–70ms.

liam: I’ll grab kernel traces and do flamegraphs in the next hour. if it’s the tokenizer mutex I can prototype a lock-free path.

sasha: FYI I bumped kv.prefetch_size 64->128 on canary nodes; initial look: fewer cold misses, but CPU up ~5–7%.

ops-bot: canary deploy mbatch-v2 -> nodes [r-i-12, r-i-13] at 10:14 UTC — success. alert: one p99 spike on r-i-13 at 10:22 for ~90s; auto-fallback didn’t trigger because mapping for mbatch-v2->mbatch-v1 was missing.

maya: noted. @taylor can you follow up on auto-fallback mapping / missing rule in rollout config? I’ll add a unit test to catch regressions.

taylor: on it. opened a small ticket and queued a docs blurb for the oncall runbook.

ken: quick ask — can we try `KV_HIT_PREFETCH=1` env on the canary? sasha thinks it’s low risk.

sasha: +1, will patch and run a 30m soak starting in 10m.

liam: if prefetch helps we should consider bumping defaults, otherwise we default back to conserving CPU. I’ll also send a short PR to remove that tokenizer mutex if traces point there.

maya: blockers: need kernel review on PR #4832 before I can promote this rollout. pinged @ken in the review thread. otherwise no blockers from my side.

ken: reviewing now, hope to merge by EOD. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks — will monitor canary for the next 60m and report any regressions.

sasha: posting quick soak metrics after 30m and will share a short table in-thread.

ops-bot: reminder — oncall pager will get a notification if p99 > 200ms for >5m. set threshold for this canary to 250ms to reduce noise during experiments.
